chapter: Civil liberties, family and the press
title: How it all fits: civil liberties and Justice Brennan on the First Amendment
summary: Hentoff says all his writing is about people becoming themselves, citing Brennan's favorite part of the Bill of Rights.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Nat, to go back to your career, the problem is – and it’s a lovely problem to have – that whenever I ask a question about your career we wind up to references to all these things and I go off on tangents.
To me they’re all part of the same piece.

Anything I write about has to do with what it is that makes people transcend themselves as they become more of themselves. That’s why civil liberties is so important. The only – I once asked Justice Brennan – whom I got to know pretty well – what was really a corny question. I said, “What’s your favorite part of the Bill of Rights?” He said, “It has to be the First Amendment, because if you can express yourself, if you can petition the government, if you can say what you want to say, if you have free exercise of religion, then everything follows from that.” That is what I write about in terms of politics and civil liberties and the like. When you’ve got a government that makes people afraid to be themselves, to say who they are, then we’re all in trouble, because eventually that becomes part of the conditioning of another generation that follows.
